jewelry.name: necklace
jewelry.title: necklace
jewelry.reason: A beaded necklace with an iron scraper/knife pendant, attributed by the museum to the Mbukushu people of Namibia; beadwork with metal pendant is consistent with their known material culture.

jewelry.name: leg-band; ornament
jewelry.title: leg-band; ornament
jewelry.reason: Two coiled leg-bands made of hair/fiber wrapped strands with glass beads, a plausible traditional personal ornament matching the museum's attribution to the Mbukushu people.

jewelry.name: bracelet
jewelry.title: bracelet
jewelry.reason: A bracelet made of bundled giraffe tail hair with copper beads, a well-known Southern African adornment type; museum attributes it directly to the Mbukushu.

jewelry.name: head-ornament
jewelry.title: head-ornament
jewelry.reason: The image shows a fibre-woven head-ornament, plausibly made and worn by the Mbukushu people of Namibia as the museum records; nothing contradicts this attribution.

jewelry.name: ring; ornament
jewelry.title: ring; ornament
jewelry.reason: A woven ring/bracelet made of plant fiber strung with light-colored seed/shell-like beads, attributed by the museum to Mbukushu maker—consistent with traditional personal adornment from this Namibian/Kavango region people.

jewelry.name: hair-pin
jewelry.title: hair-pin
jewelry.reason: A carved wooden hair-pin with a geometric-incised head, attributed by the museum to Mbukushu makers — a personal adornment item consistent with the claimed people's material culture.

jewelry.name: ornament
jewelry.title: ornament
jewelry.reason: A pair of hair ornaments made of glass beads and bean/nut-shell pendants on fibre thread, matching the museum's attribution to the Mbukushu as makers of a personal adornment item.

jewelry.name: leg-band; ornament
jewelry.title: leg-band; ornament
jewelry.reason: A beaded leg-band of hair, leather and copper beads, attributed by the museum to Mbukushu makers — a plausible personal ornament worn by this people.

arms.name: arrow
arms.title: arrow
arms.reason: Two iron-tipped arrows with wood shafts and feather fletching, consistent with weapons made and used by the Mbukushu of the Okavango region; the museum credits Mbukushu manufacture directly.
